title: Tharinda, Ron and Vinuka star in David Pieris Groups’ 8-wicket win | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 30 July 2026 03:56
-     - 1

Tharinda Nirmal captured six wickets for David Pieris Group of Companies

By P.D. De Silva

Tharinda Nirmal captured six wickets while Ron Chandraguptha smashed 83 off 66 balls and  Vinuka Rubasinghe chipped in with an unbeaten 44 of 75 balls to steer David Pieris Group of Companies to an eight-wicket win in their MCA Premier League match against Nawaloka Hospitals, played at the MCA ground on Tuesday.

Nawaloka Hospitals electing to bat first were restricted to 137 by Tharinda Nirmal (6/28) and Dilanka Anwardt (2/15). Sameen Kandanarachchi and Dilshan Arambegedara were the top scorers for Nawaloka with 34 and 31 runs respectively.

In the chase, Ron Chandraguptha smashed 83 off 66 balls with nine boundaries and four sixes  while Vinuka Rubasinghe contributed an unbeaten 44 off 75 balls with three hits to the ropes to steer the  David Pieris team to an eight wicket win in the 26th over.

David Pieris Group lead the points table with two wins in two outings.

Scores:

Nawaloka Hospitals 137/10 in 35.5 overs (Sameen Kanadanarachchi 34, Dilshan Arambegedara 31; Tharinda Nirmal 6-28, Dilanka Anwardt 2-15) vs. David Pieris Group of Companies 139/2 in 25.4 overs (Ron Chandraguptha 83, Vinuka Rubasinghe 44*; Prasad Rathnayaka 2-37)

title: All Island Elite U-18 Sevens in Central Province | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 30 July 2026 03:54
-     - 1

By Shamseer Jaleel

The All Island Under-18 Schools Rugby Sevens 2026 will be worked off on 8 and 9 August at the Trinity College Rugby Stadium in Pallekele.

There will be 24 teams playing in eight groups on day one, while day two will move on to the knockout stages. The majority of these players will feature in the 2027 rugby season for their respective schools. Wesley are the defending champions, having got the better of D.S. Senanayake College in the final. 

Group A: Wesley College, Ananda College, Richmond College

Group B: Isipathana College, Mahanama College, St. Sylvester's College

Group C: St. Joseph's College, Science College, Sri Rahula College

Group D: St. Peter's College, Dharmaraja College, St. Aloysius' College

Group E: Kingswood College, Thurstan College, Lumbini College

Group F: Zahira College, St. Anthony's College, Lalith Athulathmudali College

Group G: Trinity College, Vidyartha College, Sri Sumangala College, Panadura

Group H: D.S. Senanayake College, Sri Sumangala College, Kandy, Maliyadeva College

title: Seylan Bank’s Mercantile victories reinforce strong internal culture of employee-centricity | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 30 July 2026 03:52
-     - 1

Seylan Bank recently celebrated the successes of its employees who won acclaim at recent national-level Mercantile sports competitions, reaffirming the Bank’s commitment to elevating holistic employee development, teamwork, and well-being beyond the workplace.

The Seylan Rugby Team’s long-awaited return to the Mercantile Rugby 7’s Tournament, after a 13-year hiatus, was met with a resounding victory. Emerging as the unbeaten champions of the 2025 Bowl Championship with a commanding 33–0 final victory, the team’s achievement builds on a proud legacy of landslide triumphs that began with historic Cup victories in 2006 and 2007. 

In addition to securing 11th place among 44 competing companies, Seylan Bank set new milestones in its extensive history of excellence in athletics. Thisath Movindu was recognised as the Best Athlete in the Novices Men’s category of the 40th Mercantile Athletics Championships, setting a new meet record in the High Jump, while Chamika Weerawardena established a new meet record in the 400m Championship category. Furthermore, Seylan’s 25-member athletics contingent achieved an impressive overall medal tally, securing 8 gold medals, 2 silver medals, and 9 bronze medals.

Seylan Bank Sports Club President and Chief Transformation and AI Officer Varuna Koggalage praised the athleticism demonstrated by Seylan’s employees.

 “It is a core belief at Seylan Bank that integrating team spirit and perseverance in the face of challenges results in exceptional personal growth. The successes of our employees at both the Athletics and Mercantile Rugby 7’s mirrors how our internal values drive our victories as an organisation,” he said. 

“Recognising excellence in the striking of a balance between career mobility and competitive sports, our Director/CEO, Ramesh Jayasekara, celebrates these victories as symbols of Seylan’s culture of high performance, resilience, and shared purpose,”  Koggalage added.

The Bank’s support for employee participation in sports forms part of its broader ‘people-first’ philosophy, which prioritises work-life balance, personal growth, and overall well-being. By encouraging participation in competitive and collaborative pursuits outside the workplace, Seylan Bank highlights its continued investment in employee engagement and holistic development, reinforcing its position as an organisation that values talent, passion, and achievement in all forms.

title: FHIIT targets corporate wellness market with Orion City expansion | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 30 July 2026 03:48
-     - 1

By Michelle Therese Alles

Functional fitness brand FHIIT has expanded to Orion City, bringing its training concept to over 15,000 professionals in one of Colombo’s largest office hubs.

FHIIT Founder Yohan Rathnayake said corporate wellness was emerging as a significant business opportunity in Sri Lanka as companies are prioritising employee mental and physical wellbeing amid rising healthcare costs. 

Rathnayake said businesses were investing in preventative health measures because they improved workforce wellbeing and productivity.

“FHIIT selected Orion City because it provides direct access to one of Colombo’s largest professional communities, bringing fitness closer to where people work,” he said.

The new facility features modern equipment, professionally designed training programmes and experienced coaches who work closely with members to ensure every session is purposeful.

The company is expanding its corporate wellness initiatives through its Ignite programme, which partners with organisations to improve employee health and wellbeing. 

Beyond corporate wellness, FHIIT Co-founder Emi Senevirathna said the company aims to establish itself as Sri Lanka’s leading training hub for HYROX, a global fitness racing competition combining endurance running and functional fitness challenges, by investing in specialised race-simulation programming, functional training equipment and coaching to prepare athletes for international competition.

Senevirathna added that FHIIT takes a different approach to functional fitness through its proprietary High Intensity Active Rest Training (HIART) methodology. “There are many gyms and fitness centres, but we did something different by bringing in the whole element of fun. Our workouts are designed to make people feel like they’re not working out,” he said. 

Rathnayake said building a strong community remained central to FHIIT. “People have lost 20 to 30 kg and tell us they’ve come off medication. That’s what matters,” he said. 

FHIIT plans to open a new outlet in Negombo before exploring opportunities in other regional and international markets.
